title: Light and Optics: Reflection, Refraction, and Lenses

questions.question: The image formed by a plane mirror is:
questions.rationale: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect image as far behind the mirror as the object is in front, with left and right swapped.

questions.question: Vehicle rear-view mirrors are convex because they:
options: Give a wide field of view with erect, small images
questions.rationale: Convex mirrors diverge light, always forming small, erect, virtual images with a wide field of view — ideal for spotting traffic behind.

questions.question: In the lesson's worked example, an object 30 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm forms an image at:
questions.rationale: 1/v = 1/20 − 1/30 = 1/60, so v = 60 cm — a real, inverted image of magnification −2.

questions.question: Which medium in the lesson's chart has the highest refractive index?
questions.rationale: Diamond's n = 2.42 is the highest listed, so light travels slowest in it and bends most.

questions.question: Stars twinkle because of:
options: Atmospheric refraction through shifting air layers
questions.rationale: Changing air density keeps bending starlight slightly differently, so the star's apparent position and brightness flicker.

questions.question: An optical fibre transmits light along a bent glass thread by:
questions.rationale: Light striking the fibre wall beyond the critical angle reflects totally, staying trapped inside — the backbone of internet cables.

questions.question: The power of a lens is measured in:
questions.rationale: Lens power P = 1/f (f in metres) is expressed in dioptres (D).

questions.question: A convex lens of focal length 25 cm has a power of:
questions.rationale: P = 1/f = 1/0.25 m = +4 D; the convex (converging) lens takes a positive power.

questions.question: When white light passes through a prism, the colour deviated the most is:
questions.rationale: Refractive index rises with frequency across the ROYGBIV spectrum, so violet bends most and red least.

questions.question: Hypermetropia (long sight) is corrected using a:
questions.rationale: The hypermetropic eye forms images behind the retina, so a converging lens pulls the focus forward onto it.
